title: Murder Over Mars

agent_0.name: Inspector Elara Voss
agent_0.appearance: Tall, lean woman in her late 30s with close-cropped silver hair, sharp grey eyes, and a thin scar across her left eyebrow. Wears a charcoal Interplanetary Constabulary coat over practical black trousers. Carries a worn leather case of forensic instruments.
agent_0.secretGoal: Solve the murder and identify the killer.
agent_0.personality: Methodical, dryly witty, and unflappable. Speaks in measured sentences and notices details others overlook. Dislikes small talk and pretense. Maintains an almost unsettling calm in chaotic situations.
agent_0.relationship: Professional authority figure; answers only to the Constabulary Council. No prior ties to the station crew or stakeholders.

agent_1.name: Dr. Cassius Wren
agent_1.appearance: A broad-shouldered man in his mid-50s with a thick salt-and-pepper beard, deep-set brown eyes, and calloused hands stained with mineral residue. Wears a rumpled geologist's field jacket over a thermal shirt. A geological hammer hangs from his belt.
agent_1.secretGoal: Murder Margaret Ashworth because she was about to expose his falsified mineral assay reports to the Interplanetary Trade Council, which would have destroyed his career and sent him to a penal colony
agent_1.personality: Charismatic and erudite, with a quick temper that surfaces when cornered. Genuinely passionate about geology but deeply insecure about his reputation. Prone to grandiose claims and dismissive of those he considers beneath him.
agent_1.relationship: Reports to Captain Blackwood; in a bitter professional rivalry with Margaret Ashworth over assay authority and reporting lines.

agent_4.name: Dr. Yuki Tanaka
agent_4.appearance: A compact woman in her early 40s with warm brown skin, dark hair tied back in a practical bun, and ink-stained fingers. Wears a green utility jumpsuit with a hydroponics division patch. Small freckles dot her nose and cheeks.
agent_4.secretGoal: Steal the proprietary gene-seed samples from the hydroponic vault to sell to a rival terraforming corporation
agent_4.personality: Gentle, curious, and quietly stubborn. Speaks softly but with unexpected firmness when her research is threatened. Finds comfort in living things and distrusts those who treat them as mere commodities or profit centers.
agent_4.relationship: Reports to the station's scientific director; has a quiet professional respect for Wren but resents being overlooked in budget allocations.

agent_5.name: Felix Drummond
agent_5.appearance: A round, ruddy-faced man in his late 30s with a receding hairline, nervous eyes, and a perpetual sheen of sweat. Wears an ill-fitting pinstripe suit that looks out of place aboard a space station. Fidgets constantly with his gold cufflinks.
agent_5.secretGoal: Embezzle the quarterly dividend payments from the mining consortium to cover his gambling debts on Earth
agent_5.personality: Voluble, anxious, and desperately image-conscious. Tries too hard to appear wealthy and connected. Hides a deep sense of inadequacy behind bravado, expensive cologne, and an overabundance of handshakes.
agent_5.relationship: A minority investor in the consortium; in a fragile partnership with Ashworth that he fears is about to dissolve, leaving him with worthless shares.

agent_2.relationship: Primary financial backer of the station; in a power struggle with Captain Blackwood over operational control of the mining operations.

agent_3.secretGoal: Frame Dr. Wren for embezzling colony funds to protect the station's funding and his own command position
agent_3.personality: Stoic, duty-bound, and quietly paranoid. Speaks in clipped, authoritative sentences. Carries the weight of command like a physical burden. Deeply loyal to his crew but suspicious of outsiders and corporate interference.
agent_3.relationship: Employed by the consortium but answers to the Interplanetary Maritime Authority; in a tense power dynamic with Ashworth over who ultimately controls the station.

agent_2.name: Margaret Ashworth
agent_2.appearance: A striking woman in her early 60s with platinum-blonde hair swept into a severe chignon, cold blue eyes behind thin-rimmed spectacles, and an impeccably tailored ivory suit. Wears a diamond signet ring and a small Mars-shaped brooch at her collar.
agent_2.secretGoal: Expose the falsified mineral reports to the Interplanetary Trade Council and revoke the station's operating license to consolidate the colony under direct consortium management
agent_2.personality: Imperious, calculating, and ruthlessly efficient. Commands a room without raising her voice. Views people as assets or liabilities. Genuinely believes she is the only one competent enough to manage the colony's future.
agent_2.relationship: Primary financial backer of the station; in a power struggle with Captain Blackwood over operational control of the mining operations.

agent_1.name: Dr. Cassius Wren
agent_1.appearance: A broad-shouldered man in his mid-50s with a thick salt-and-pepper beard, deep-set brown eyes, and calloused hands stained with mineral residue. Wears a rumpled geologist's field jacket over a thermal shirt. A geological hammer hangs from his belt.
agent_1.secretGoal: Murder Margaret Ashworth because she was about to expose his falsified mineral assay reports to the Interplanetary Trade Council, which would have destroyed his career and sent him to a penal colony
agent_1.personality: Charismatic and erudite, with a quick temper that surfaces when cornered. Genuinely passionate about geology but deeply insecure about his reputation. Prone to grandiose claims and dismissive of those he considers beneath him.
agent_1.relationship: Reports to Captain Blackwood; in a bitter professional rivalry with Margaret Ashworth over assay authority and reporting lines.

agent_0.name: Inspector Elara Voss
agent_0.appearance: Tall, lean woman in her late 30s with close-cropped silver hair, sharp grey eyes, and a thin scar across her left eyebrow. Wears a charcoal Interplanetary Constabulary coat over practical black trousers. Carries a worn leather case of forensic instruments.
agent_0.secretGoal: Solve the murder and identify the killer.
agent_0.personality: Methodical, dryly witty, and unflappable. Speaks in measured sentences and notices details others overlook. Dislikes small talk and pretense. Maintains an almost unsettling calm in chaotic situations.
agent_0.relationship: Professional authority figure; answers only to the Constabulary Council. No prior ties to the station crew or stakeholders.

agent_6.name: Sera Okafor
agent_6.appearance: A sharp-featured woman in her mid-30s with close-shorn black hair, warm dark eyes, and a confident smile that rarely reaches her eyes. Wears a sleek black communications officer's uniform with a journalist's press badge pinned to her collar.
agent_6.secretGoal: Blackmail Captain Blackwood with evidence of his unauthorized communications with the Martian separatist movement
agent_6.role: Station Communications Officer / Embedded Journalist, Interplanetary Press
agent_6.personality: Quick-tongued, perceptive, and morally flexible. Asks questions that make people deeply uncomfortable. Genuinely believes in the story but will bend the truth if it serves her narrative or her byline.
agent_6.relationship: Embedded with the station by editorial contract; has a complicated professional history with Captain Blackwood from a previous assignment that left both of them wary.

agent_5.name: Felix Drummond
agent_5.appearance: A round, ruddy-faced man in his late 30s with a receding hairline, nervous eyes, and a perpetual sheen of sweat. Wears an ill-fitting pinstripe suit that looks out of place aboard a space station. Fidgets constantly with his gold cufflinks.
agent_5.secretGoal: Embezzle the quarterly dividend payments from the mining consortium to cover his gambling debts on Earth
agent_5.personality: Voluble, anxious, and desperately image-conscious. Tries too hard to appear wealthy and connected. Hides a deep sense of inadequacy behind bravado, expensive cologne, and an overabundance of handshakes.
agent_5.relationship: A minority investor in the consortium; in a fragile partnership with Ashworth that he fears is about to dissolve, leaving him with worthless shares.

agent_4.name: Dr. Yuki Tanaka
agent_4.appearance: A compact woman in her early 40s with warm brown skin, dark hair tied back in a practical bun, and ink-stained fingers. Wears a green utility jumpsuit with a hydroponics division patch. Small freckles dot her nose and cheeks.
agent_4.secretGoal: Steal the proprietary gene-seed samples from the hydroponic vault to sell to a rival terraforming corporation
agent_4.personality: Gentle, curious, and quietly stubborn. Speaks softly but with unexpected firmness when her research is threatened. Finds comfort in living things and distrusts those who treat them as mere commodities or profit centers.
agent_4.relationship: Reports to the station's scientific director; has a quiet professional respect for Wren but resents being overlooked in budget allocations.

agent_3.name: Captain Theron Blackwood
agent_3.appearance: A tall, gaunt man in his late 40s with a weathered face, steel-grey eyes, and a rigid military bearing. Wears a pressed navy officer's uniform with brass insignia. A thin scar runs from his right temple to his jaw.
agent_3.secretGoal: Frame Dr. Wren for embezzling colony funds to protect the station's funding and his own command position
agent_3.personality: Stoic, duty-bound, and quietly paranoid. Speaks in clipped, authoritative sentences. Carries the weight of command like a physical burden. Deeply loyal to his crew but suspicious of outsiders and corporate interference.
agent_3.relationship: Employed by the consortium but answers to the Interplanetary Maritime Authority; in a tense power dynamic with Ashworth over who ultimately controls the station.

room_0.name: The Grand Rotunda
room_0.description: A vast circular chamber at the very heart of the station, where the great axis of rotation hums like a sleeping god beneath one's feet. Polished brass railings spiral upward along the curved walls, and a chandelier of cold white filaments casts a steady, shadowless glow over the marble floor. The air carries the faintest scent of ozone and old varnish. Every corridor, every passage, every private quarter radiates outward from this central point like the spokes of a wheel, so that one cannot walk three steps in any direction without arriving, inevitably, at another soul. It is here that the dead man was found, slumped in a leather armchair as though merely dozing, his wine glass still warm in his hand.

room_7.name: The Spoke Gallery
room_7.description: A long, narrow corridor that connects the Grand Rotunda to the outer rim, running the full diameter of the station like the spoke of a great wheel. The floor is inlaid with alternating strips of dark walnut and pale birch, and the walls are lined with small, evenly spaced portholes through which the black of space and the red of Mars alternate in a slow, hypnotic rhythm. Overhead, a single continuous strip of soft light runs the gallery's full length, casting every face in a flat, unforgiving pallor. The rotation makes the air feel subtly different at each end, a gentle pressure against the eardrums that reminds one, with quiet insistence, that one is suspended in the void. It is the most-travelled path aboard, and the most likely place in which to be seen, or not seen, at the critical moment.

room_6.name: The Mining Archive
room_6.description: A windowless, climate-controlled vault where the colony's geological surveys, ore-yield projections, and financial ledgers are stored in rows of steel filing cabinets that stretch into a dim, blue-lit distance. The air is dry and carries the sharp, metallic tang of oxidised iron samples pinned to display boards. A single desk lamp throws a cone of warm light over a reading surface, and the rest of the room recedes into a penumbra where the cabinets stand like the pews of a secular cathedral. The silence here is absolute and total, broken only by the soft tick of the cooling fans and the occasional creak of a drawer sliding open. Every document in this room is a thread in a web of profit and obligation, and the dead man's name appears in no fewer than forty-seven of them.

room_5.name: The Hydroponic Conservatory
room_5.description: A long, vaulted greenhouse where the station's botanists coax pale, elongated plants from trays of engineered soil beneath banks of ultraviolet grow-lights. The air is thick, green, and faintly sweet, tasting of chlorophyll and damp earth, a shocking luxury after the sterile corridors. Vines of trailing ivy climb the support struts, and a small fountain trickles in the centre, its water catching the violet light in prismatic shards. It is the only place aboard where one might, for a moment, forget the vacuum pressing against the hull. The glass panels are frosted with condensation, and the sound of dripping water provides a soft, rhythmic counterpoint to the station's mechanical breathing. A place where one might hide a body beneath a bed of ferns, or a secret beneath a layer of loam.

room_4.name: The Captain's Study
room_4.description: A compact, book-lined chamber at the station's innermost ring, where the gravity is gentlest and the hum of the axis is most pronounced. A heavy oak desk dominates the room, its surface buried beneath navigational charts, sealed correspondence, and a single glass of brandy gone to a cloudy amber. The walls are lined with shelves of leather-bound volumes and framed certificates of command, and a portrait of the Captain's predecessor stares down with an expression of perpetual, weary disapproval. A locked drawer, a private telephone, and a small sidearm in a walnut case complete the inventory of authority. The door, when closed, seals with a satisfying hydraulic thud that sounds, to the uninitiated, rather like a coffin lid settling into place.

room_3.name: The Crew's Mess
room_3.description: A rectangular compartment of brushed steel and bolted plating, where the station's engineers, technicians, and service staff take their meals at long communal tables. The walls are scarred with tally marks and faded crew rosters, and the overhead fluorescents flicker with an irritating, arrhythmic buzz. The smell of reconstituted coffee and salted protein rations clings to the air like a second skin. A battered radio crackles in the corner, broadcasting a tinny waltz from a world none of them will see again for months. The chairs are bolted to the floor, and the food is served in identical grey trays. It is a place of honest exhaustion, of aching backs and the quiet, shared dignity of those who keep the machine alive while others count their shares.

room_2.name: The Stakeholders' Salon
room_2.description: A long, low-ceilinged drawing room furnished with an almost aggressive opulence that seems grotesque against the utilitarian bulkheads beyond its doors. Persian carpets, smuggled at great expense, muffle the footsteps of silk slippers. The walls are lined with framed portraits of the colony's founders, their painted eyes following one with proprietary interest. A crystal decanter of single-malt whisky sits perpetually on a side table, and the air is thick with the mingled perfumes of expensive cologne and the particular mustiness of enclosed wealth. Here the investors gather to discuss quarterly returns over sherry, their laughter bright and brittle as the glass they clink together. Every smile in this room has a price attached, and every handshake conceals a ledger.

room_1.name: The Observatorium
room_1.description: A domed chamber at the station's outermost rim, its entire ceiling a single pane of reinforced crystal through which the rusted, pocked face of Mars fills the sky in terrible, beautiful detail. The red dust storms swirl in slow, silent processions below, and the mining colony's searchlights blink like the eyes of buried insects. Velvet drapes, heavy and wine-dark, frame the viewing arches, and a long mahogany telescope rests on its brass mount, cold to the touch. The rotation of the station lends the view a gentle, perpetual drift, as though one is watching the world turn in a slow, indifferent waltz. It is a room for contemplation, for secrets whispered to a planet that will never answer.
